title: The Godfather
facts: Francis Ford Coppola directed the film and wrote the screenplay with Mario Puzo, from Puzo's 1969 novel.
The Godfather won three Academy Awards: Best Picture, Best Actor, and Best Adapted Screenplay.
Marlon Brando declined his Best Actor Oscar. Sacheen Littlefeather spoke at the ceremony on his behalf.
Cinematographer Gordon Willis was nicknamed "The Prince of Darkness" for his shadowy lighting.
Al Pacino, James Caan, and Robert Duvall were all nominated for Best Supporting Actor for this film.
The cat in Don Corleone's lap in the opening scene was a stray found on the studio lot.
The baby in the baptism scene is Sofia Coppola, the director's daughter.
Talia Shire, who plays Connie Corleone, is Francis Ford Coppola's sister.
The words "Mafia" and "Cosa Nostra" are never spoken in the film.
The Sicily scenes were filmed in the villages of Savoca and Forza d'Agrò, not in the town of Corleone.
The Godfather opened in the United States in March 1972.
In 1990 the Library of Congress selected The Godfather for the National Film Registry.
Lenny Montana, who plays Luca Brasi, was a former professional wrestler.
John Cazale, who plays Fredo, appeared in five feature films. All five were nominated for Best Picture.
The Godfather Part II (1974) also won the Academy Award for Best Picture.
